title: Whole Double Envelope and Continuous Cristae Mitochondrion
description: One wholly newly authored enlarged mitochondrial cutaway: a complete bean-like outer envelope surrounds a distinct inner boundary membrane which folds continuously inward into seven alternating broad cristae. All crista faces and their rounded returns belong to one connected inner-membrane mesh, with actual open cut-section channels communicating toward the intermembrane groove; they are not floating plates, separate stacks or repainted chloroplast grana. The upper roof is intentionally removed to show the architecture, and a low opaque basal section supports this teaching representation. One whole education model, zero scenes, four restrained opaque membrane and cut-surface material roles. Broad cut-open junctions, wall thickness, count and scale are schematic: no exact species or tissue, measured nanoscale anatomy, narrow native junction aperture, membrane bilayer, matrix-fluid volume, DNA, ribosome, ATP synthase, respiration, dynamics, molecular interaction or physical-stability claim. Nothing from old chloroplast domain geometry is reused. No textures, transparency, labels, rig, animation or biological simulation.
